title: Dublin Glasco watchmakers
standfirst: Newspaper notices and a trade directory preserve a small Dublin watchmaking circle. Occupation and addresses make it a useful documentary cluster, but not a proved family tree.
question: Can a primary record connect the Dublin watchmakers and distinguish the competing Thomas profiles?
answer: Philip Glasco senior and junior are separately reported as watchmakers. The 1779 Christchurch Lane marriage notice and the 1783 Ormond Quay directory very probably concern one Thomas watchmaker. No inspected source states his relationship to either Philip or supports the attached Thomas chain.

chapters.title: Two named Philips
body: A 1750 marriage notice calls Philip Glasco senior an eminent watchmaker of Christchurch Lane; a 1760 notice reports his wife's death.
A younger Philip, also a Christchurch watchmaker, married Teresa Plunkett in 1768 and died in Christ Church Lane in 1770. The notices do not state the two men were father and son.

chapters.title: One likely travelling address
body: A 1779 notice places Thomas Glasco, watchmaker, at Christchurch Lane when he married Miss Hynes of Ormond Quay. Watson's 1783 directory lists Thomas Glasco, watchmaker, at 20 Ormond Quay.
The uncommon name, occupation and apparent move to the bride's street strongly support one tradesman. They do not identify him with any existing Thomas profile.

clusters.title: Christchurch Lane watchmakers
clusters.summary: Notices separately record senior and junior Philip Glasco as watchmakers at Christchurch.
clusters.boundary: The notices do not state their relationship or connect them to Thomas.

clusters.title: Thomas, watchmaker
clusters.place: Christchurch Lane and Ormond Quay, Dublin
clusters.summary: The same occupation, rare surname and compatible addresses make the 1779 and 1783 Thomas occurrences a close match.
clusters.boundary: No primary record links this tradesman to the three competing Thomas profiles or proves serial marriages.

links.label: shared trade and Christchurch setting; no stated kinship

proved: The named newspaper and directory occurrences.
supported: The 1779 and 1783 Thomas entries likely describe one watchmaker.
hypothesis: Thomas belonged to the wider Glasco watchmaking circle.
unresolved: Which, if any, existing Thomas profile is the watchmaker.

gaps.title: Find probate and parish records
gaps.why: They may name spouse, children or other watchmakers.

gaps.why: They could distinguish masters, apprentices and addresses.
